info.title: SENA ai_chatbot gateway
info.description:
Single production entry point for the SENA assistant (Flutter mobile / React web).

**One endpoint, chip-driven routing.** The frontend sends every message to `POST /api/route` with the tapped chip in `context.category`; the gateway routes it to the right backend section and streams the answer back as Server-Sent Events. There is no free-text classification — no chip means out of scope.

**Sections are independent:** a `shifts` request can never reach client data, and vice-versa.

**SSE events:** `meta` (routing) → `token` (answer) → `usage` (input/output token counts for the question) → `done`; or `error`.

get.description: The gateway is a JSON routing API now — no UI. Point clients at /api/route.

post.summary: Route a chip-selected message and stream the answer (SSE)
post.description:
Route one chip-selected message to the right backend section and stream the reply.

**Auth:** `Authorization: Bearer <JWT>` (the ISENA token). The gateway forwards
it to the backend, which validates it.

**Routing:** decided by `context.category` (shifts / client / policy /
procedure). No category → out of scope (the stream returns a single guidance
message). Sections are independent — a `shifts` message cannot return client data.

**Example**

```
POST /api/route
Authorization: Bearer <JWT>
{"question": "What are my shifts this week?", "context": {"category": "shifts"}}
```

parameters.name: authorization

schema.description: Bearer <JWT> — the ISENA token from POST /auth/ai/login.
schema.title: Authorization

parameters.description: Bearer <JWT> — the ISENA token from POST /auth/ai/login.

401.description: Missing or invalid Authorization bearer token.

question.title: Question
question.description: The user's message. May be empty when a chip is tapped with no text — the section's default question is used.
examples: What are my shifts this week?

context.title: Context
context.description: UI context. Must include `category` (the tapped chip). May also carry session_id / session_title / is_new_chat.

RouteRequest.title: RouteRequest
RouteRequest.description:
A user message plus the UI context that selects how it is routed.

Routing is chip-driven: `context.category` decides the backend section. There
is no free-text classification — a request with no category is out of scope.

`context.category` values:
  • "shifts"    → staff service, STAFF section  (shifts, rosters, team)
  • "client"    → staff service, CLIENT section (participant info)
  • "policy"    → policy service                (organisational policy)
  • "procedure" → policy service                (compliance procedures)

examples.question: What are my shifts this week?
